item.q: Dominic is observing a volvox colony and a paramecium under a microscope. He makes a note in his journal that the volvox colony and the paramecium are similar because they have many organelles for movement. What would Dominic most likely notice about the movement of a volvox colony and a paramecium?
choices: They both move at the same rate.
They both move away from light.
They both move in the same direction.
They both move toward an energy source.

item.q: Estuaries are dynamic ecosystems where salt water and fresh water mix. Usually this happens as fresh water flows from a river to an ocean. When would you expect the concentration of salt in the estuary water to be LOWEST near the mouth of the river?
choices: when the river flow is low and the tide is low
when the river flow is high and the tide is low
when the river flow is low and the tide is high
when the river flow is high and the tide is high

item.q: A party shop delivers helium-filled balloons to homes and businesses. The owners realize from experience that on hot summer days they should inflate the balloons only three-quarters full. On cold winter days they can fully inflate the balloons. Which of the following is the best hypothesis to explain this observation?
choices: The helium gas is more active in the winter season.
Air outside the balloons leaks into the balloons.
As the temperature increases, the helium in the balloons expands.
Outdoor air pressure in the summer is less than indoor air pressure.

item.q: Nearly 100 years ago, a large volcano erupted in the South Pacific. The following year, Boston recorded measurable snow every month of the year, and most of the Northern Hemisphere experienced a cold summer. Which explains how these two events were related?
choices: The eruption intensified the greenhouse effect.
Lava flow from the eruption caused a temporary increase in Earth's total heat energy.
The eruption caused damage to the ozone layer.
Air pollution from the eruption caused a decrease in the amount of solar energy reaching Earth.

item.q: A student is using a straw to blow bubbles into a calcium hydroxide solution. The carbon dioxide in the student's breath is reacting with the water to form an acid, which begins to neutralize the basic solution. Which of the following best describes the initial change in pH of the solution?
choices: increase in pH toward a pH of 7
increase in pH away from a pH of 7
decrease in pH toward a pH of 7
decrease in pH away from a pH of 7

item.q: Devil facial tumor disease (DFTD) is a disease that is decimating the population of Tasmanian devils. The disease passes from one animal to another through bites and is caused by parasites. The parasites cause cancerous tumors that spread throughout an infected animal's body and kill it. What is the best description of DFTD?
choices: a non-infectious, cell-cycle disease
an infectious, cell-cycle disease
a non-infectious, chronic disease
an infectious, chronic disease

item.q: The force of an object, with a certain mass accelerating at a certain rate, can be determined by using the equation below. force = mass x acceleration Which object would have the greatest force?
choices: a 5-kg object accelerating at 10 m/s^2
a 5-kg object accelerating at 20 m/s^2
a 20-kg object accelerating at 4 m/s^2
a 20-kg object accelerating at 3 m/s^2

item.q: Students heated three objects to different temperatures during a classroom demonstration. Each object emitted light of a different color as shown below. Object 1: blue light Object 2: red light Object 3: orange light Which list presents the objects in order from highest to lowest temperature?
choices: Object 1, Object 2, Object 3
Object 1, Object 3, Object 2
Object 2, Object 1, Object 3
Object 2, Object 3, Object 1

item.q: In your garden, you want to plant marigolds all around your pepper plants because you read that this flower repels whiteflies. How can you test to see if marigolds really do repel whiteflies?
choices: Count the number of whiteflies on the peppers before and after planting marigolds.
Count the number of whiteflies on the marigolds near the peppers.
Kill the whiteflies on other plants in the garden except on the peppers.
Put whiteflies on other garden plants and see what happens.

item.q: Which statement best describes the process of respiration?
choices: Oxygen and sugar are used in the process that provides energy to cells; water and carbon dioxide are its waste products.
Water and sugar are used to in the process that provides energy to cells; oxygen and carbon dioxide are its waste products.
Oxygen and carbon dioxide are used in the process that provides energy to cells; sugar and water are its waste products.
Carbon dioxide and sugar are used in the process that provides energy to cells; water and oxygen are its waste products.

item.q: Each student in Ms. Jordan's science class was given a beaker containing several substances that had been stirred thoroughly. Maxwell must classify the contents of his beaker as either a compound or a mixture. Which of the following would indicate that the beaker contains a mixture?
choices: The original substances had different densities.
The contents of the beaker reacted to form a new substance.
The original substances had a greater mass than the contents of the beaker.
The contents of the beaker can be easily separated into the original substances.

item.q: Scientists have been able to insert genes from a spider into the genome of a domestic goat. When the goat matures, it produces milk that contains a protein found in spider webs. This protein can then be extracted and used to make strong but lightweight materials for bulletproof vests, automobiles, and aircraft. The change does not cause the goat any pain, but some people think that it is not right to add genes from the genome of one animal to another. Which word best describes this concern?
choices: economic
biological
ethical
practical

item.q: The students in a class would like to make 20 paper sailboats for a race. The students will select one design and collect the materials they need to construct the boats. Which of the following is the best way for the students to be sure the paper sailboats will float without tipping over in the water?
choices: construct a prototype of a boat for testing
calculate the total mass of all of the finished boats
determine the total amount of weight each boat can carry
test the strength of each material used to construct the boats

item.q: A science class is studying the states of matter. One group of students freezes 100 grams (g) of water in a cup. Another group of students melts 50 g of ice in a cup. Which of these will most likely occur at the end of the experiment?
choices: The temperature of both cups will be the same.
Both samples in the cups will be in the same state.
Both groups will have the same mass with which they started.
The time required for the changes in states of matter will be the same.

item.q: A euglena cell has a structure called an eyespot that detects light. A paramecium does not have an eyespot, and so it cannot detect light. Why doesn't a paramecium need an eyespot?
choices: A paramecium does not live where there is light.
A paramecium does not photosynthesize its own food.
A paramecium lives in shallower water than a euglena.
A paramecium uses cilia instead of a flagellum to move.

item.q: People without safe drinking water may get an illness called dysentery. Dysentery is caused by a type of amoeba that lives inside the body. Doctors can find these amoebas by looking at body samples under a microscope. Which characteristic of amoebas best explains why doctors use microscopes to find dysentery amoebas?
choices: Amoebas can change their shape.
Amoebas need humans to survive.
Amoebas look just like human cells.
Amoebas are made of only one cell.
